summary: Service-permission boundary enforcement prevents ephemeral SA delegation for batch deploy rollback
description:
Issue summary: A recent org-wide permission-boundary enforcement policy started blocking sts:AssumeRole chains used by ephemeral service accounts created during batch deploy rollback workflows. Impact: Several automated rollback jobs for Dedicated and Private deploy pipelines are failing to acquire delegated credentials. This results in rollback aborts and delayed restoration of stable model versions for a small subset of customers on dedicated pools.

Impact detail: - 5 rollback pipelines failed between 2026-03-09 22:00 and 2026-03-10 03:00 UTC. - Visible customer impact limited to dedicated tier customers in us-east-1 using pinned model versions; no data plane leakage observed. - Automated retries hit authorization denied errors and then timed out, requiring manual intervention.

Environment: Production (deploy-runner, dedicated provisioner, sts broker, org-perm-policy v2.1), us-east-1.

Observed behavior: When the rollback job requests an ephemeral SA via the provisioner, the broker attempts a chained AssumeRole to a cross-account debug role. The final AssumeRole returns AccessDenied with error message: "permission boundary condition evaluation failed: policy prohibits role session with tag 'deploy-type=batch'". Prior to the org policy upgrade this chain worked normally.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Trigger a batch deploy rollback in the deploy-runner against a dedicated cluster in us-east-1. 2) Observe the provisioning logs for ephemeral SA creation. 3) Watch the sts broker -> assume-role chain and note the first AccessDenied from the target account. 4) The deploy-runner marks the rollback as failed after exponential backoff (~15 minutes).
logs:
Excerpt from sts-broker logs (2026-03-10T01:12:04Z):
- Request: AssumeRole(RoleArn=arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/redwood-deploy-proxy, SessionTags={deploy-type=batch,commit=abc123,env=prod})
- Response: AccessDenied: Permission boundary condition evaluation failed for resource arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/redwood-deploy-proxy.
Stack traces: deploy-runner: auth: failed to proxy role assume: AccessDenied
Related cloud-trace link: https://console.aws.amazon.com/cloudtrail/home?region=us-east-1#events:eventId=abcd-ef01
investigation_notes: Checked recent org policy rollover on 2026-03-09; new policy enforces that role/session tags must match an allowlist and rejects unknown tags via condition matching.
Confirmed deploy-runner adds a 'deploy-type' session tag set to 'batch' for batch rollbacks. This tag is not in the org policy allowlist for the target account role.
Verified other flows (ad-hoc debug assume-role without 'deploy-type' tag) succeed, indicating the tag is the differentiator.
Reproduced failure in a staging mirror by toggling the policy to deny on unknown tags; identical AccessDenied returned.
Hypothesis: Policy change was intended to reduce lateral movement risk but did not account for automated orchestration flows that add operational tags.
Temporary mitigation applied: a fine-grained exception was created for the deploy-proxy role in the target account to allow session tags matching 'deploy-type=batch' for a 12 hour window.
comments: Priya Nair (Reporter) 2026-03-10: Initial alert from deploy-runner after three consecutive rollbacks failed. Escalating to IAM/oncall.
Liam Chen (Assignee) 2026-03-10: Reproduced in staging. Linking org-policy rollout PR. Will coordinate with Security to scope an exception runway.

Ava Martinez (Security) 2026-03-11: Policy intent acknowledged. We need a long-term solution that preserves tag-based controls while letting orchestrated rollbacks function. Suggests creating an ops-principal allowlist instead of broad tag exceptions.
Samir Patel (SRE) 2026-03-12: Applied 12h exception on target account and monitored; rollbacks resumed successfully. No further auth errors observed during window.

Liam Chen 2026-03-13: Drafting infra PR to update deploy-runner to add a 'role:orchestrator' tag and request ops allowlist entry; filing follow-up infra change to normalize session tag schema across provisioner and broker.
resolution_notes:
Temporary fix: added targeted allowlist entry in target account's permission boundary evaluation to permit session tag 'deploy-type=batch' for role arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/redwood-deploy-proxy for 12 hours, enabling pending rollbacks to complete.
Long-term fix: two-part plan: (1) Update deploy-runner and sts-broker to emit standardized tag 'actor=orchestrator' instead of variable 'deploy-type' variants and add a signed allowlist check for ops principals. (2) Update org policy documentation and run a controlled rollout with Security to whitelist orchestrator principal ARNs rather than tags.
Follow-ups (action items):
- INT-272010: infra PR to normalize session tag naming across provisioner and broker (owner: Liam Chen).
- INT-272011: Security change request to create an ops-principal allowlist and retire permissive tag exceptions (owner: Ava Martinez).
- Monitor: SRE to watch rollback metrics for 72 hours post-fix and confirm no regressions.
notes: This ticket is internal-impacting (affects internal rollback automation) but customer-facing rollbacks for dedicated customers were impacted transiently; coordinate comms if any customer-reported incidents surface.
